attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own published essay, written in his voice.

semantics.note: Firm wording ('cannot, under any circumstances'). Read in context, it is a conditional claim about the industry after OpenAI fails. The antecedent 'without OpenAI' is kept and no horizon is added.

contract.note: Reading 'without OpenAI' as OpenAI ceasing operations, and survival as continued material commercial activity, is an ordinary plain reading. The contract adds no deadline. Its point that one collapse cannot prove 'any circumstances' is reasonable and does not decide this outcome.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own status page shows services running on Oct 27, 2026. That counts against the antecedent (cessation), not against the conditional claim, so it is context only.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm conditional forecast with no deadline. The antecedent, OpenAI ceasing operations, has not happened: the evidence shows it still operating as of Oct 27, 2026. There is no post-cessation record to test industry survival, so the claim cannot be scored yet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own first-person prediction in his essay.

semantics.note: 'I think these are an inevitability' expresses certainty about the outcome, not graded doubt, so it is scored as a forecast. 'These' supports reading it as both events. The historical lead-in ('has never faced') is correctly left unscored. No deadline is stated.

contract.note: Requiring both events, and established facts rather than allegations, follows the plural 'these' and is an ordinary reading. The contract correctly holds that continued operation cannot contradict an open-ended prediction. The '2027' mentioned nearby is rightly not treated as this sentence's deadline.

evidence.note: Court order in Apple's suit filed July 10. It covers allegations and breach claims against the individual defendants, with no finding that OpenAI breached its own contract or failed to pay. Context only.

reviews.rationale: No deadline is stated. The packet establishes neither an OpenAI payment failure nor an OpenAI breach of a major-company contract after publication. No event has closed off the possibility either. The forecast stays open.

attribution.note: Zitron's own prediction in his essay.

semantics.note: Firm 'will', conditioned on the previous sentence: hyperscalers stop spending and banks pull back. The normalised claim keeps that antecedent, both labs, and the open 'at some point' horizon.

contract.note: Reading the antecedent as a broad spending and lending retrenchment, and requiring both labs to seek money during that same episode, is a fair ordinary reading. The contract flags the difference between a literal stop and a slowdown.

evidence.note: Anthropic says it filed an S-1 on Oct 26. That shows IPO preparation, not a qualifying pullback, and is a company statement about itself.
PIMCO's September outlook projects that debt supply will keep growing. It is a projection, not a measured lending pullback.
Meta's Q2 2026 capex figure covers one company in a quarter mostly before the post. It cannot establish an industry-wide pullback.

reviews.rationale: Whether the antecedent happened (hyperscalers stopping spending, banks pulling back) is unknown. Nothing in the packet shows such a retrenchment, or both labs seeking money during one. Under the policy an unknown antecedent is not scored, and the horizon is open.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his essay.

semantics.note: Firm claim that a meaningful capex slowdown pushing NVIDIA below 60%+ growth is enough for NVIDIA to stumble, with a stated sentiment cause. The normalised claim keeps the 60% threshold and has no horizon.

contract.note: Comparing quarterly revenue year over year is a reasonable reading of 'year-over-year revenue bumps', and it is flagged. Treating 'stumble' as a material setback is an ordinary reading. Requiring evidence for the 'because' mechanism is strict, but that cause is part of the statement.

evidence.note: NVIDIA's 10-Q (unaudited) shows Q2 FY27 revenue up 106% year over year, far above 60%. So the antecedent had not occurred in that quarter. Context only.

reviews.rationale: The antecedent is not shown to have occurred: NVIDIA's latest verified quarter grew 106% year over year, and there is no documented capex slowdown. No deadline is stated. Strong growth before the antecedent does not contradict the claim, so it cannot be scored yet.
